title: WASSCE Further Maths: Calculus (Differentiation & Integration) - Further Mathematics - Gradients of Tangents
subject: Further Mathematics

questions.q: Find the gradient of the tangent to the curve $y = x^3 - 2x^2 + x$ at the point where $x=2$.
questions.explain: The gradient is given by $\frac{dy}{dx}$. Differentiating gives $\frac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2 - 4x + 1$. Substituting $x = 2$, we get $3(2)^2 - 4(2) + 1 = 12 - 8 + 1 = 5$.

questions.q: Find the exact gradient of the curve $y = 5x^2 - 3x + 2$ at the point where it crosses the y-axis.
questions.explain: The curve crosses the y-axis when $x = 0$. The gradient function is $\frac{dy}{dx} = 10x - 3$. Substituting $x = 0$ gives a gradient of $-3$.
questions.subject: Further Mathematics

questions.q: Find the gradient of the curve $y = 4x - x^2$ at $x = 1$.
questions.explain: The gradient is determined by evaluating the derivative $\frac{dy}{dx}$ at the given point. $\frac{dy}{dx} = 4 - 2x$. Substituting $x = 1$ gives $4 - 2(1) = 2$.

questions.q: Find the gradient of the horizontal line $y = 5$ at any point on the curve.
questions.explain: The gradient is represented by the derivative of the function. The derivative of a constant (like $y=5$) is $0$, reflecting that the horizontal line has no slope or steepness.
